title: Rapoport Says Saquon Barkley’s Hamstring Injury Leaves Him ‘Week‑to‑Week’: NBC Sports Update
body:
The Philadelphia Eagles’ dynamic running back Saquon Barkley will miss at least the next few games after a hamstring strain forced him out of the team’s latest matchup, and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport confirmed that the veteran is now being classified as a “week‑to‑week” player. The designation means medical staff will continue to evaluate his injury daily, but there is no guarantee he will be back for the upcoming Thursday night contest against the New York Giants, let alone the remainder of the season.

Barkley’s injury came at a critical juncture for Philadelphia, which is currently perched near the top of the NFC East and fighting to solidify a playoff berth. The 27‑year‑old, who signed a lucrative four‑year, $72 million extension last summer, has already amassed 1,200 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns in just seven games this year. His ability to break off big runs and serve as a dual‑threat receiver has been a cornerstone of the Eagles’ offensive game plan. Without him, head coach Nick Sirianni will be forced to rely more heavily on backup running backs Miles Sanders and Kenneth Gainwell, both of whom have shown flashes of productivity but lack Barkley’s blend of power and elusiveness.

The hamstring issue is not new for Barkley, who has missed significant time in each of his first three NFL seasons due to similar injuries. This pattern has raised concerns among analysts about his long‑term durability and the wisdom of the Eagles’ massive financial commitment. However, the team’s medical staff remains optimistic, noting that Barkley’s conditioning regimen and the early stage of the strain suggest a relatively swift recovery. “We’re monitoring him closely and will make a decision based on his response to treatment,” a spokesperson told reporters, echoing Rapoport’s “week‑to‑week” assessment.

From a strategic standpoint, Barkley’s absence forces the Eagles to adjust their offensive balance. In the past two seasons, Philadelphia has leaned heavily on its aerial attack, with quarterback Jalen Hurts posting a career‑high passer rating and the squad ranking among the league’s top passing offenses. Yet the run game still accounts for roughly 40 percent of total yardage, and Barkley’s presence forces defenses to respect the ground attack, opening up play‑action opportunities for Hurts. Without that threat, opposing secondaries may stack the box, potentially limiting Hurts’ deep‑ball efficiency and putting extra pressure on the receiving corps, which includes standout talents like A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith.

The ripple effects extend beyond the Eagles’ own roster. The NFC East division rivals—particularly the Giants and Dallas Cowboys—will be watching closely, as a weakened Philadelphia offense could shift the balance of power in the conference. Moreover, the injury adds another variable to the already complex playoff picture, where each win or loss can dramatically alter seedings and home‑field advantage. Fantasy football owners, too, will feel the impact; Barkley has been a top‑tier running back pick this season, and his uncertain status will likely cause a flurry of roster moves across leagues.

Looking ahead, the Eagles’ medical team will continue daily assessments, with the goal of returning Barkley to the field as soon as it is safe. If the hamstring heals without setback, the running back could rejoin the lineup within two to three weeks, just in time for the pivotal stretch run that determines postseason positioning. In the meantime, the coaching staff will need to devise creative schemes to compensate for the loss, perhaps by integrating more quarterback draws and leveraging the versatility of their backup backs. As the season edges toward its climax, the Eagles’ ability to adapt without their marquee rusher will be a key storyline, and the league will be watching to see whether Saquon Barkley can bounce back and reclaim his role as one of the NFL’s most electrifying playmakers.
